decision: began a full implementation round from mokmok-os-architecture.md in a worktree off origin/main (be7e131)
why: the requested deliverable is a working pass over the target crate map, and a worktree keeps the tree that carries it separate from the shared checkout

decision: froze the round as the twelve target crates, so seven new crates plus expansions of two landed ones
why: the repository already split state-machine and sandbox out of the grouped plan, so finer boundaries match the trajectory the architecture doc allows

decision: registered all seven new members and their dependencies in one commit before any crate work started
why: concurrent writers to one manifest would race, and a valid workspace at the branch tip lets every delegate build against the same base

decision: wrote the kernel config unit as the first verifiable piece rather than waiting on the seven writers
why: the command line is the one boundary the kernel owns alone and it compiles against clap only, so the wait costs nothing

decision: seven crate writers ran at once, each in its own worktree, against the frozen interface
why: disjoint crate directories are a clean seam, and one writer per manifest removed the only shared mutable file
result: six crates green on their own gate; the observability writer died to a harness error and its worktrees branch was completed by hand

decision: merged the seven branches one at a time, running the workspace gate after each
why: each unit proves itself before the next lands on it, and a break is localized to the merge that caused it
result: clippy and tests green after each; one load-sensitive flake in mokmok-sandbox/tests/supervision did not reproduce in three isolated runs

decision: added Access::union to the sandbox rather than a table of the seven access triples in the kernel
why: the kernel needed to name what it decided as one set, and the shape assumption belongs to the crate that owns the set
result: clippy and the sandbox suite green

decision: drove the vertical slice through mokmokd from an integration test: artifact hash, supervisor directory, subscriber over the bus
why: the acceptance predicate is about what a caller can observe, not about the kernels own types

decision: ran the mutation gate on the three new pure crates and got 76%, 88%, and 89%, all below the workspace's 95% floor
why: a rule nothing can falsify is a rule the suite does not test, and the survivors pointed at the specificity ordering, the terminal-state table, and untested renders
result: three gaps recorded, each fixed by tests rather than suppression

decision: three delegate runs closed the gaps: protocol 98.6%, scheduler 100%, capability 100%
why: each delegate reran the real gate on the committed tree, so the numbers are measured rather than claimed
result: one protocol survivor is provably equivalent and left in place

decision: left the kernels own mutation gate unscored and fixed the reason instead
why: its baseline could not build the sandbox confiner, which belongs to another package, so the gate failed before testing a mutant; the error that hid this was a Display that dropped the cause
result: recorded as open work: scoring the kernel needs the gate to build the workspace, not the package
